samples.summary: Flipping the Yorkie auth webhook's enforcement default is unrelated scope bundled into the notes share-link parity issue (#1044)
samples.evidence: The stated issue this branch implements is notes share-link toolbar parity (docs/design/notes/notes.md "Share-link parity", "issue #1044"). Alongside it the branch changes a deployment-wide security posture: `isYorkieAuthEnforced` makes anything but the literal `false` enforce, rewriting the documented staged rollout (docs/design/yorkie-auth-webhook.md steps 2/3 now invert: shadow becomes opt-in, enforce becomes the default) and changing behaviour for every existing deployment that has the variable unset — those were deliberately in shadow so "a resolver bug can't lock everyone out during rollout" (yorkie-auth.controller.ts handleAuth comment). That is a separate, operationally risky change whose blast radius (share links, revision history, template gallery, existing installs) has nothing to do with mounting a toolbar on the notes share route, and it forecloses the reversible rollout the design doc committed to. It deserves its own change so it can be reviewed and released on its own.

samples.summary: `readOnlyNoteStore` duplicates `readOnlyDocStore`'s Proxy machinery verbatim instead of sharing it; the two copies have already diverged
samples.evidence: packages/docs/src/store/read-only.ts (lines 67-169) and the new packages/notes/src/store/read-only.ts implement the same security-sensitive wrapper: identical non-configurable-descriptor carve-out in `get`, identical `set`/`defineProperty`/`deleteProperty`/`getPrototypeOf`/`setPrototypeOf`/`preventExtensions`/`isExtensible`/`has`/`getOwnPropertyDescriptor`/`ownKeys` traps, identical memoization map and `batch` passthrough, differing only in the readers allowlist and the `undo`/`redo` null return. Nothing was extracted into `@wafflebase/core` (packages/core/src has only image/geometry/tokens/url and packages/notes does not depend on core), so a fix or trap gap found in one copy must be found again in the other. They have already diverged: the notes copy adds `READ_ONLY_VIEWS` idempotence and `HISTORY_METHODS`, which the docs copy lacks — so "is this handle already guarded?" and "what does undo return under read-only?" now have two different answers for the same boundary. The repo's stated expectation is reuse (shared code in `@wafflebase/core`; Slides reuses the Docs engine).

samples.summary: The public-template-gallery precondition now passes with the variable unset, weakening a gate whose documented job was to require an affirmative "enforcing" configuration
samples.evidence: `assertYorkieAuthEnforced` previously accepted only `'true'` — an explicit operator acknowledgement that the webhook is enforcing (its doc comment still reads "requires the Yorkie auth webhook to be **enforcing**, not merely configured", lines 62-64). After this change it returns for `undefined`, `''`, `'1'`, `'yes'` and anything not literally `false`. Registering the webhook methods on the Yorkie project remains a manual, unverified step (yorkie-auth.controller.ts doc: "with none registered Yorkie never calls this endpoint and nothing here runs"), so a deployment that never registered them and configured nothing now sails through the gate while no per-document check exists at all — exactly the state the gate was written to refuse, with the documented consequence that anonymous visitors edit every public template and one request per card flushes the gallery into a human-only review queue.

samples.summary: Canonical design docs still state shadow mode is the default; only notes.md and yorkie-auth-webhook.md were updated
samples.evidence: docs/design/sharing.md:208-235 still says enforcement "is **off by default**. `YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE` is unset in a stock deployment, which puts the controller in shadow mode" and builds its whole risk section on the client-side `readOnly` flag being the write boundary in the default configuration. The same stale claim survives in docs/design/template-gallery.md:668 ("with `YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE` unset the auth webhook only…"), docs/design/revision-history.md:504, and docs/design/docs/docs-image-editing.md:301. After this change those are wrong, so the repo gives two answers to "does a stock deployment enforce?" — the point the branch says most needs to be unambiguous. The repo files docs by subsystem and expects the canonical doc to be folded, not left contradicting a sibling.

samples.summary: Comments added by this same change assert the old shadow-by-default posture it removes
samples.evidence: packages/notes/src/view/editor.ts:447 (added in this diff) states "the Yorkie auth webhook ships in shadow (allow-all) mode by default and so may not refuse the write either", and the new packages/notes/src/store/read-only.ts:64 states "the webhook allows everything until a deployment both registers its methods and sets `YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE=true`". Both contradict the backend half of the very same change (`isYorkieAuthEnforced`: enforcing is the default, only literal `false` opts out) and the doc rewrite in docs/design/yorkie-auth-webhook.md. A reader of the notes engine is told the opposite of the deployment reality.

samples.summary: Engine divider restyling (7px → 25px, `touch-action`, drag-ratio math) is a separate concern from share-link toolbar parity and changes the workspace route's desktop layout
samples.evidence: The diff widens the split divider from 7px to 25px, adds `box-sizing`, `touch-action: none`, and rewrites the drag ratio to measure against `rect.width - divider.offsetWidth`. None of it is needed for the share-link parity outcome (which is fixed by mounting `NotesToolbar` and demoting `both` on mobile), and it visibly alters the existing workspace notes split view for every user. It also stakes a claim on the host app's CSS reset ("stated rather than inherited because the host app's CSS reset decides it otherwise"), i.e. engine code reasoning about frontend styling. Reasonable work, but it belongs in its own change rather than riding along.

samples.summary: `SharedNotesLayout` re-implements `notes-detail`'s state trio and mobile `both`→`edit` demotion rather than sharing a hook
samples.evidence: notes-detail.tsx:90-120 holds the same `viewMode`/`keymap`/`showAuthors` state initialised from the same `read*` helpers and the same `isMobile && viewMode === 'both' ? 'edit' : viewMode` demotion; shared-notes-layout.tsx:53-70 copies both. The only intended difference is that the shared route never persists. A small shared hook (read-once state + demotion, with an opt-out of the writers) would keep the two entry paths from drifting again — which is precisely the drift issue #1044 was about.

finding.summary: Flipping the Yorkie auth webhook's enforcement default is unrelated scope bundled into the notes share-link parity issue (#1044)
finding.evidence: The stated issue this branch implements is notes share-link toolbar parity (docs/design/notes/notes.md "Share-link parity", "issue #1044"). Alongside it the branch changes a deployment-wide security posture: `isYorkieAuthEnforced` makes anything but the literal `false` enforce, rewriting the documented staged rollout (docs/design/yorkie-auth-webhook.md steps 2/3 now invert: shadow becomes opt-in, enforce becomes the default) and changing behaviour for every existing deployment that has the variable unset — those were deliberately in shadow so "a resolver bug can't lock everyone out during rollout" (yorkie-auth.controller.ts handleAuth comment). That is a separate, operationally risky change whose blast radius (share links, revision history, template gallery, existing installs) has nothing to do with mounting a toolbar on the notes share route, and it forecloses the reversible rollout the design doc committed to. It deserves its own change so it can be reviewed and released on its own.

verdict.reason: The code is present as described (isYorkieAuthEnforced enforces unless the literal 'false'), but the reasons that make it a *major* design-fit violation are contradicted by the repository. (a) The rollout is not foreclosed: docs/design/yorkie-auth-webhook.md:201-209 keeps shadow mode as an explicit rollout step and states "Reversible at every step: flip the flag back, or unregister the webhook methods to fully disable"; yorkie-auth.controller.ts:95-105 and logPosture() (:134-147) preserve and announce the shadow option; unregistered methods still mean no enforcement (:102-105, doc :199-200), so the blast radius is limited to installs that already registered webhook methods. (b) Design-doc discipline was followed, not broken: the canonical subsystem doc was updated in place with rationale (yorkie-auth-webhook.md:29-32, :224-234) rather than a parallel doc. (c) The change is not unrelated to #1044: docs/design/notes/notes.md:306-328 (§Share-link parity) makes the webhook default the explicit server-side counterpart of mounting an editable toolbar for share-link viewers, stating the client-side read-only mounts bound only this app and that "enforcement is the default, so only an explicit YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE=false turns it back off" (:321). Under this lens's rubric no acceptance criterion of #1044 is unmet (todo N1-N8 all checked), no logic is duplicated, and no stated Non-Goal is crossed (yorkie-auth-webhook.md:45-52; the "safe, reversible rollout" Goal at :43 is preserved). What remains is a "should have been its own PR" process point whose cost stays inside the codebase — minor, which does not block. The behavioral denial risk belongs to the correctness lens, which already graded it non-blocking.

verdict.reason: Verified directly: packages/notes/src/store/read-only.ts:93-185 reproduces packages/docs/src/store/read-only.ts:67-169 nearly verbatim — same non-configurable/non-writable descriptor carve-out in `get` (docs:84-87 vs notes:112-115), same non-function hiding (docs:96 vs notes:117), same {raw,view} memoization (docs:71,98-99 vs notes:98,119-120), same `batch` passthrough (docs:110-112 vs notes:134-136), and equivalent set/defineProperty/deleteProperty/getPrototypeOf/setPrototypeOf/preventExtensions/isExtensible/has/getOwnPropertyDescriptor/ownKeys traps (docs:122-167 vs notes:149-180). Nothing was extracted: packages/core/src holds only image/geometry/tokens/url, and packages/notes/package.json:52-71 has no @wafflebase/core dependency. The claimed divergences exist (notes-only READ_ONLY_VIEWS at notes:43,94,183 and HISTORY_METHODS at notes:35,125-126), though the undo difference is justified by the interface (DocStore.undo(): void at packages/docs/src/store/store.ts:87-88) and the idempotence difference by notes wrapping at two sites (packages/notes/src/view/editor.ts:249, packages/frontend/src/app/notes/notes-view.tsx:152) vs docs' one (packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:1075). I considered refuting as out-of-scope via docs/design/shared-core-extraction.md:46-48 ("Store abstraction unification" Non-Goal) and docs/design/notes/notes.md:289-291 (documents the copy as a deliberate "sibling"), but that Non-Goal concerns unifying store *interfaces* into a common base, which a generic allowlist-driven proxy helper would not require, and a doc acknowledging the copy does not make it non-duplicative. Copied write-boundary trap logic must be fixed twice, a cost beyond internal tidiness, so I cannot concretely refute under any named ground.

finding.summary: The public-template-gallery precondition now passes with the variable unset, weakening a gate whose documented job was to require an affirmative "enforcing" configuration
finding.evidence: `assertYorkieAuthEnforced` previously accepted only `'true'` — an explicit operator acknowledgement that the webhook is enforcing (its doc comment still reads "requires the Yorkie auth webhook to be **enforcing**, not merely configured", lines 62-64). After this change it returns for `undefined`, `''`, `'1'`, `'yes'` and anything not literally `false`. Registering the webhook methods on the Yorkie project remains a manual, unverified step (yorkie-auth.controller.ts doc: "with none registered Yorkie never calls this endpoint and nothing here runs"), so a deployment that never registered them and configured nothing now sails through the gate while no per-document check exists at all — exactly the state the gate was written to refuse, with the documented consequence that anonymous visitors edit every public template and one request per card flushes the gallery into a human-only review queue.

verdict.reason: The gate reads the same predicate the webhook itself uses, so the state the finding describes cannot arise. `assertYorkieAuthEnforced` (template-review.ts:79-86) calls `isYorkieAuthEnforced` (yorkie-auth-enforcement.ts:20-21), and `YorkieAuthController` sets its own posture from the identical call (yorkie-auth.controller.ts:121-125), with the shadow/allow-anyway branch gated on `!this.enforce` (line 156). With the variable unset the webhook HONOURS denials, so an unset deployment is enforcing, not shadowing — the gate still refuses exactly the configurations (`'false'`) in which a preview token would also grant writes, which is its documented job (template-gallery.md:673). The coupling is deliberate and asserted (template-review.spec.ts:49-63: "a stricter reading here would shut the gallery on a deployment that is in fact enforcing"). The manual method-registration gap the finding leans on is orthogonal and unchanged: the old `=== 'true'` reading never verified registration either (yorkie-auth.controller.ts:102-105 — the variable "only chooses whether a computed denial is honored"; yorkie-auth-webhook.md:28-32). What genuinely remains is stale prose in docs/design/template-gallery.md:368 and :668 that predates the enforce-by-default flip recorded in the canonical yorkie-auth-webhook.md:29-31 — design-doc staleness with behavior unchanged, which this lens grades minor and non-blocking, not the major gate weakening claimed.
